# Dubbla fullträffar för Öresund – förvaltaren om frakteuforin

**Feed**: borslunch  
**Published**: 2026-10-21  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

EFN Börslunch with guest Anders Wennberg from Öresund's management team covered the Q3 report season, where expectations look stretched: strong companies are falling on good numbers and weak ones are bouncing on okay reports, with DSV as the example. Wennberg was negative on Thule because its durable products have saturated its market. He likes Ovzon on European defence demand and is happy with Scandi Standard, though he now sees it as fully valued. He said to take profits in Frontline at peak tanker rates and suggested a defensive tilt via Essity, Carlsberg, Royal Unibrew, Orkla and Sampo.

---

## Universe Stocks

### ⛔ THULE — Thule | **AVOID** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Negative | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Guest: durable products saturated the market during Covid; no replacement cycle for many years; consensus darling status is a warning sign.

#### Reasoning

Guest opinion (Anders Wennberg, Öresund). Fund managers misread demand: roof boxes and bike racks last ~20 years, so Covid pulled demand forward for many years. 'Everyone owns it' status signals the case is fully discovered. Governance turmoil (chairman ousted). Report due tomorrow.

#### Sell Triggers

- evidence of a new replacement cycle
- strong organic growth in the upcoming report

> *"De har för bra produkter. De har ju mättat sin marknad under corona, inte minst med takboxar och cykelställ."*

---

### 🟢 OVZON — Ovzon | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 70%

Öresund holding; pure defence, almost debt-free, good Q3 orders; SpaceX's actions against Ukraine highlight Europe's need for its own satellites.

#### Reasoning

Guest owns it via Öresund (stated bias). Thesis: European defence needs non-US satellite capacity after SpaceX restricted Ukraine. 100% defence customers and a clean balance sheet versus Eutelsat. Order intake is lumpy, but Q3 was good with delayed H1 orders landing.

#### Sell Triggers

- order intake stalls
- Europe does not prioritise sovereign satellite capacity

> *"Jag tror att det kommer att bli ett ökat intresse för Ovzon och kanske även JutelSat."*

---

### 🟠 ETL — Eutelsat | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Could benefit from European satellite demand, but more debt and a declining TV broadcasting business.

#### Reasoning

Guest: 'maybe not a top company'; mixed LEO/GEO, heavy debt, declining broadcasting legacy; may see more interest on the European sovereignty theme.

#### Sell Triggers

- debt concerns intensify
- broadcasting decline accelerates

> *"Det är kanske inget toppenbolag"*

---

### 🟠 DSV — DSV | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Up 9% on an in-line report after heavy pessimism; keeps its 9bn Schenker synergy target; guest likes the M&A integration model.

#### Reasoning

Guest likes the concept (among the world's best acquirers/integrators) and admits he too feared Schenker was too much. Report roughly as expected, weaker in Road, better in Air & Sea. No valuation view or explicit buy call.

#### Sell Triggers

- Schenker synergy target cut
- integration delays worsen

> *"Jag gillar konceptet. De är kanske en av världens bästa på att göra de här förvärven."*

---

### 🟡 SCST — Scandi Standard | **HOLD** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Öresund holding; 2.72 SEK/kg EBIT heading past the 3 SEK target; ~14x EBIT feels fully valued but should grow into it.

#### Reasoning

Guest: no longer cheap or a turnaround, but volume growth, margin expansion from under-utilised Dutch and Lithuanian plants, and the Irish acquisition mean it becomes cheap again over time. Structural buyers (Lantmännen, a Portuguese owner) keep buying.

#### Sell Triggers

- margin progress toward 3 SEK/kg stalls
- volume growth reverses

> *"Det är ett bra bolag och på sikt kommer det växa in i sin värdering och bli billigt igen."*

---

### 🔴 FRO — Frontline | **SELL** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 70%

Rates at an extreme spike; guest: 'as good as it gets', sell half again; huge dividends are the counterargument.

#### Reasoning

Guest earlier said to own tankers, then to sell half; now says sell half of what remains. Disruption-driven rates normalise as shipowners optimise the fleet and oil arbitrage narrows. Dividends could be about a third of market cap over 6-9 months, so trim rather than exit.

#### Sell Triggers

- rates fall rapidly
- Hormuz disruption resolves

> *"Om du fortfarande har nåt kvar, ska du sälja hälften igen. Det är, tror jag, as good as it gets."*

---

### 🟠 DHT — DHT | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 45%

Cheaper crude tanker alternative to Frontline.

#### Reasoning

Guest: DHT is cheaper, an alternative to Frontline, but the same peak-rate caveat applies.

#### Sell Triggers

- tanker rates normalise

> *"DHT är billigare, så det kan man ha som ett alternativ."*

---

### 🟠 TRMD-A — Torm | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Product tankers: diesel inventories tighter than crude; peace could boost refined product volumes from the Gulf.

#### Reasoning

Guest suggests product tankers (Torm, Hafnia) as an alternative to crude tankers; less downside on peace than Frontline/DHT; 'can't sleep well, but a bit better'.

#### Sell Triggers

- diesel inventories normalise

> *"Man kan inte sova jättegott om natten med den, men lite bättre."*

---

### 🟠 HAFNI — Hafnia | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 45%

Product tanker alternative, same thesis as Torm.

#### Reasoning

Same as Torm: refined product tightness and a possible peace volume boost from Gulf refineries.

#### Sell Triggers

- diesel inventories normalise

> *"Torm och Hafnia är de två stora i Norden"*

---

### 🟢 ESSITY-B — Essity | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Defensive pick: P/E 13, strong brands (TENA, Libero), Gardell bought in; guest says the stock has become a bit too cheap.

#### Reasoning

Guest suggests making portfolios more defensive ahead of a possible AI correction. Essity has a low valuation and strong segment brands; the structural risk is share loss to private label.

#### Sell Triggers

- accelerating share loss to private label

> *"Jag tycker att aktien har blivit lite väl billig."*

---

### 🟢 CARL-B — Carlsberg | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Defensive: P/E 12-13, good brands, shifting mix toward soft drinks and non-alcoholic beer; won the Pepsi contract.

#### Reasoning

Guest: 'I like Carlsberg'. Adapts its product mix as beer drinking falls; reasonable valuation for a defensive portfolio.

#### Sell Triggers

- volume decline outpaces mix shift

> *"Jag gillar Carlsberg, och man kan även ta Royal Unibrew."*

---

### 🟢 RBREW — Royal Unibrew | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

Sold off after losing the Nordic Pepsi contract; now P/E 12, 'on sale'; further along in the product transformation.

#### Reasoning

Guest sees the sell-off as overdone; leads the transformation away from traditional beer; defensive at a low multiple.

#### Sell Triggers

- further contract losses

> *"Ja, men nu köper den till rea."*

---

### 🟢 ORK — Orkla | **BUY** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 50%

Grocery brands; slow private-label share loss but the valuation has come down a lot.

#### Reasoning

Guest includes it in the defensive basket; the structural headwind is offset by a lower valuation.

#### Sell Triggers

- private-label share loss accelerates

> *"Men nu har värderingen kommit ner så långt."*

---

### 🟢 SAMPO — Sampo | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 60%

P/E ~15, down from 18-20 on AI-disruption fears; guest unconvinced given its data advantage and regulatory barriers.

#### Reasoning

Guest argues AI shopping agents won't easily disrupt it: price comparison already exists, Sampo (If, Topdanmark, Hastings) has deep risk data, and capital requirements deter new entrants. Multiple contraction looks unwarranted.

#### Sell Triggers

- AI-driven distribution erodes pricing power

> *"Men jag är inte säker på det."*

---

### 🟠 CA — Carrefour | **WATCH** (Weak)

**Sentiment**: Mixed | **Time Horizon**: MT  
**Confidence**: 40%

Guides down due to unrest in France, but P/E 8 'cheap actually'.

#### Reasoning

Host/guest note it is cheap even before estimate cuts; they did not return to it as a full pick.

#### Sell Triggers

- deeper estimate cuts
- prolonged unrest in France

> *"Den är billig faktiskt."*

---
